title_en: Shanghai No. 7 Construction Engineering Company v. Bank of Communications, Hainan Branch — dispute over compensation for fraudulent withdrawal of deposit

full_text_en:
Shanghai No. 7 Construction Engineering Company v. Communications Bank of China, Hainan Branch — dispute over compensation for deposit wrongfully withdrawn

Plaintiff: Shanghai No. 7 Construction Engineering Company, Hainan Company.

Legal Representative: Ling Lifu, Manager.

Agents ad litem: Wang Xurong and Zeng Ying, lawyers from New Oriental Law Firm.

Defendant: Communications Bank of China, Hainan Branch.

Legal Representative: Quan Jushan, President.

Agent ad litem: Guo Jianjun, lawyer from Shenghé Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Shanghai No. 7 Construction Engineering Company, Hainan Company (hereinafter referred to as the Construction Company), filed a lawsuit with the Xinhua District People's Court of Haikou City, Hainan Province, against the defendant, Communications Bank of China, Hainan Branch (hereinafter referred to as Hainan Jiaohang), over a dispute concerning compensation for damages arising from the wrongful withdrawal of its deposit.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant, Hainan Jiaohang, failed to strictly examine the seal impressions when handling the transfer business, resulting in the plaintiff's deposit being wrongfully withdrawn by another person. The plaintiff requests that the court order the defendant to compensate the plaintiff for the wrongfully withdrawn deposit of RMB 657,000 and interest losses of RMB 134,657.64.

Defendant's Defense: The plaintiff's deposit was wrongfully withdrawn by a criminal suspect using the alias Ding Zhong, who forged the seal impressions. In handling this transaction, our bank conducted a careful examination using the corner-folding verification method in accordance with banking practices and settlement regulations. It was only because the criminal method employed by the suspect exceeded our ability to discern forgeries, and even professionals from the public security departments would find it difficult to identify, that the crime succeeded. Therefore, our bank has fulfilled its duty, is not at fault, and should not bear civil liability for compensation. The plaintiff failed to properly safeguard its seal, providing the criminal with an opportunity to commit the crime, and should bear liability for its own fault.

Facts Found by the Court:

The plaintiff, the Construction Company, maintained a deposit account (Account No. 0141123090) with the defendant, Hainan Jiaohang. On November 4, 1995, a criminal suspect, using forged seals of "Shanghai No. 7 Construction Engineering Company, Hainan Company Financial Seal" and a personal seal of "Shen Weizhong," submitted a certificate to Hainan Jiaohang and purchased a book of transfer checks. On November 9, 1995, the criminal suspect again used the said forged seals to issue Transfer Check No. NO: 0359754 and submitted it to Hainan Jiaohang. After examination by the handling personnel, the transaction was processed, and RMB 657,000 was transferred from the Construction Company's account to Account No. 032178701 at Haikou City Construction Bank, under the name of Ding Zhong. On November 22, 1995, when the Construction Company inquired about the deposit balance at Hainan Jiaohang, it discovered that its deposit had been withdrawn and immediately reported the matter to Hainan Jiaohang. On November 24, 1995, Hainan Jiaohang reported the case to the Haikou City Public Security Bureau. On November 8, 1996, the Hainan Provincial Public Security Department issued Document Examination Authentication Report No. Qiong Gong Xing Ji (Wen) Zi (96) No. 66, confirming that the seals of "Shanghai No. 7 Construction Engineering Company, Hainan Company Financial Seal" and the personal seal of "Shen Weizhong" on Transfer Check No. NO: 0359754 and the certificate for purchasing the check on November 4, 1995, were forged by printing methods. During the investigation by the Haikou City Public Security Bureau, RMB 75,000 of the wrongfully withdrawn funds was recovered but has not yet been returned to Hainan Jiaohang. The remaining funds have not been recovered, and the culprit has not been apprehended.

The above facts are confirmed by the Transfer Check No. NO: 0359754 and the certificate for purchasing the check kept by Hainan Jiaohang, the Authentication Report No. (96) No. 66 of the Hainan Provincial Public Security Department, the certificate of the Haikou City Public Security Bureau, and the statements of the parties, which are sufficient to establish the facts.

Opinion of the Court:

The plaintiff, the Construction Company, opened a deposit account with the defendant, Hainan Jiaohang, and the rights and obligations of both parties are clear. Since Hainan Jiaohang accepted the Construction Company's deposit, it assumed the obligation to ensure the safety of that deposit. The fact that the Construction Company's deposit was wrongfully withdrawn by another person indicates that Hainan Jiaohang failed to fulfill its duty and was at fault. In accordance with the provisions of Article 106, paragraphs 1 and 2, of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Hainan Jiaohang shall compensate the Construction Company for the wrongfully withdrawn deposit of RMB 657,000, plus the interest that such deposit would have earned at the demand deposit rate.

The corner-folding verification method is the method for authenticating the genuineness of seals prescribed in the current "Bank Settlement Accounting Procedures Manual." This provision belongs to internal banking regulations and is binding only on bank employees. With the development of technology, the methods used by criminals are becoming increasingly numerous. Banks must continuously improve and enhance their anti-counterfeiting and authentication capabilities in response to this situation, in order to fully ensure the safety of customer deposits. If a bank voluntarily accepts customer deposits without being able to enhance its anti-counterfeiting authentication capabilities, and such deposits are subsequently wrongfully withdrawn by others using forged seals, the bank must bear liability for compensation. The defendant, Hainan Jiaohang, refused to bear compensation liability on the grounds that its staff had performed the corner-folding verification work procedures in accordance with regulations and had not discovered that the seals were forged, and therefore was not subjectively at fault for the wrongful withdrawal of the deposit. This argument is untenable.

In conclusion, the Xinhua District People's Court of Haikou City rendered the following judgment on November 27, 1998:

The defendant, Hainan Jiaohang, shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate the plaintiff, the Construction Company, in the amount of RMB 657,000, and pay interest calculated at the bank's demand deposit rate for the same period from November 9, 1995, until the date the said amount is fully repaid. If payment is overdue, the debt interest for the period of delayed performance shall be paid at double the rate.

Court costs of RMB 12,930 shall be borne by the defendant, Hainan Jiaohang.

After the first instance judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed.
